publisher: TAQA Distribution (Abu Dhabi Distribution Company PJSC)
title: Utility Tariff 2025
archive_note: The publisher's own PDF, downloaded directly, linked from the residential rates page as VIEW FULL TARIFF GUIDE.
establishes: The tariff in force from 1 January 2025, stated on the document's own face: 'This document details the utility tariffs for the different customer segments as of 1 January 2025.'
The expatriate residential water rate: AED 7.84 per 1,000 litres within the daily allowance, AED 10.41 above, with 700 litres a day for a flat and 5,000 for a villa. Identical to the 2017 booklet.

The full segment list the publisher recognises: UAE Nationals, Social Card Holders in both classes, Expats, Government, Agriculture, Industrial, Commercial, unmetered supply, tanker filling stations, recycled water, EV charging and transmission-connected customers.
A fixed charge of AED 150 a month for unmetered water supply, and no fixed or recurring charge priced for metered residential water anywhere in the document.
Recycled water at AED 1.70 per 1,000 litres for all customers, which is a separate non-potable service.
That no wastewater tariff appears in the utility's own tariff document for any segment.
does_not_establish: The VAT treatment. The document carries no VAT statement in either direction.
That the document enumerates every charge a residential bill may carry. It is a schedule of tariffs, and a bill can carry items that are not tariffs.
Whether a residential wastewater charge is levied by some other body. The absence of a wastewater tariff here is evidence about TAQA Distribution's tariffs, not about the household's bill.
reconciliations_passed: The 2017 booklet and this document give identical expatriate water rates. UAE VAT was introduced on 1 January 2018, between the two. A rate that had absorbed a 5% tax would have had to fall by 4.762%; it did not move at all.
